source:
Build a 3D obby (obstacle course) game. I explicitly want this to be a real
3D game. The player controls an avatar that walks and jumps through a course
of floating platforms, moving spinners, and gaps in a 3D world, racing to
reach the finish. Add checkpoints and a timer. Falling resets to the last
checkpoint.

image_prompt.text: A chain of floating platforms spaced to the physics limits, forming the ordered route to the finish
Gaps between platforms that have to be cleared with a running jump
Rotating spinners set along the route that sweep players off the platforms
Flat enclosed pads set at intervals where players land safely
the finish at the end of the course, visible ahead as the thing being raced toward

layout_placement.text: Respawn points that return a fallen player to the last pad reached rather than the start
a detection zone at the finish that ends the run and stops the timer

notes: No obby option carries a terminal finish trigger; the finish is written as free text in both streams.
The user asked explicitly for a real 3D game with avatar movement and camera control — worth passing on as a constraint, not a layout feature.

open_questions.ask: Nothing was said about the setting — should the platforms float in an empty sky, or over a themed world?
How long should a full run take, so the number of platforms and checkpoints can be set?

coverage_missing.ask: Empty sky, or a themed world under the platforms?
How long is a full run?
Is the timer just displayed, or are players competing on it?

answers.ask: Nothing was said about the setting — should the platforms float in an empty sky, or over a themed world?
answers.answer: Use a simple bright sky-world setting, with the course floating above clouds. Keep the focus on clear, readable 3D platforms and obstacles.

answers.ask: How long should a full run take, so the number of platforms and checkpoints can be set?
answers.answer: Target a short 3–5 minute run for a first clear. Use a small course with a few checkpoints.
